subject: BlueWave Order Form — proposed IP indemnity exclusion and cap workback
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BlueWave — Order Form/LOLI redlines

Attaching the customer's redlines (see RW-BlueWave_MSA_redlines_20260803.pdf). Key ask from BlueWave: remove the liability cap carve-out for IP indemnity from the MSA and add an explicit exclusion to consequential damages. Short summary:

- They want: “Notwithstanding Section 7.2, Vendor’s liability cap shall not apply to claims for IP infringement; Vendor shall be liable for all damages resulting from such claims.”
- They also propose removing consequential damages carveouts entirely (which would broaden recovery).

We need legal to weigh in on: risk tolerance if we agree to an unlimited IP indemnity (they're a mid-sized analytics firm), possible compromises (sub-cap for IP indemnity, defense-only carve-out, escrow/security), and commercial implications (sales/time to close).

Options I see for negotiation:
1) Reject and insist on standard carve-out language we use (IP indemnity survives cap but limited to defense costs + direct damages up to insurance limits).
2) Propose a capped exception (e.g., IP indemnity excluded from the general cap but subject to a specific sub-cap of $3M–$10M).
3) Offer indemnity with insurance-first language + escrow/deductible to limit exposure.

Can legal and ops please review — need a recommended position to present to the customer by EOD tomorrow.

Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BlueWave — Order Form/LOLI redlines

Thanks Karthik — reviewed the redlines. High level legal take: we should avoid an open-ended, unlimited IP indemnity outside of the cap. That materially increases long-tail risk and could blow past our insurance and reserved liability assumptions.

Practical compromise to propose back that balances customer need and our risk profile:

- Keep indemnity for IP infringement as an exception to the general liability cap, BUT make the exception subject to a specific sub-cap for IP indemnity. Suggested language for negotiation (redline attached RW-Proposed-IP-Workback-redline.docx):

  "Notwithstanding Section 7.2 (Limitation of Liability), Redwood's liability arising under its indemnification obligations solely for claims alleging that Redwood's deliverables infringe a third party's intellectual property rights ("IP Indemnity") shall not be subject to the general liability cap in Section 7.2. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood's aggregate liability for IP Indemnity shall be limited to the greater of (a) direct damages actually incurred up to USD 5,000,000 per claim and USD 10,000,000 in the aggregate, and (b) amounts paid by Redwood under applicable insurance policies covering such claims."

- Exclude consequential damages as customary, but clarify examples and carve in reasonable categories such as direct remediation costs and reasonable external counsel fees.

Rationale: this gives BlueWave clearer remediation certainty while bounding our maximum exposure. It also preserves our ability to rely on insurance recovery. If sales wants a smaller number to close quickly, we can consider $3M/$6M instead of $5M/$10M.

Next steps: Karthik/LAuren — do you want me to send this redline directly to BlueWave legal, or would you prefer a call to walk through? If they push for removal of the cap entirely, escalate for leadership sign-off.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Tom Hargreaves <tom.h@bluewave.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueWave Legal <legal@bluewave.com>, Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@bluewave.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: BlueWave — Order Form/LOLI redlines

Grace — thanks for the quick read. Appreciate the attempt at a middle ground. A few points from our side:

- BlueWave's position is that an IP indemnity outside the cap (without limit) is standard for us because our product integrates with sensitive customer data and IP exposure is material.
- We're open to a numeric cap but it needs to be commercially meaningful — $5M per claim still may be insufficient for some of our customers.

Attached: Annotated_OrderForm_BlueWave_v2.docx with comments. Our counter-proposal: keep the indemnity outside the general cap but include a modest sub-cap only if Redwood agrees to a second-tier remedy: Redwood must (a) use commercially reasonable efforts to defend/settle, and (b) agree to an escrow arrangement for remediation funds if a claim proceeds past a threshold.

We prefer to discuss on a quick call; I can make time tomorrow afternoon.

Tom
Head of Partnerships
BlueWave Analytics

Attachment: Annotated_OrderForm_BlueWave_v2.docx (customer redlines and commentary)

Agree with Grace's suggested approach. From a commercial POV, BlueWave is a strategic mid-market account (deal RW-2026-0472) — we want to close but not at the cost of open-ended exposure. A couple of operational asks:

- If legal is okay with $5M/$10M we should pre-approve a one-time exception path so procurement can prepare a DocuSign envelope (see link) and Finance can check insurance recoverability.
- Escrow is workable but will add ~2–3 weeks; flag to the customer early.

If customer insists on no cap, suggest we escalate to Markus and the legal ops committee for leadership approval. Otherwise I'm fine to run the compromise with them and try to land at $5M/$10M or $3M/$6M depending on their appetite.

Lauren Bishop

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Final: recommended negotiation posture for BlueWave — IP indemnity

Following internal discussion and a quick risk check with insurance: final recommended position to present to BlueWave (we can present as a single-band counter):

- IP Indemnity to be carved out of the general liability cap BUT subject to the following sub-cap:
  • Per claim: USD 5,000,000 (direct damages + reasonable defense costs)
  • Aggregate: USD 10,000,000
- Redwood will prioritize defense and remediation and will pursue insurance recovery; language will make recoveries from insurance primary where applicable.
- Escrow is acceptable as a remediation mechanism but at BlueWave's cost; it will add time to close.
- Maintain exclusion of consequential damages; clarify that direct remediation and reasonable external counsel fees are recoverable under IP indemnity.

Action items: please route the attached RW-Proposed-IP-Workback-redline.docx to the customer with the cover note above. Karthik — prepare a short call with Tom (30 minutes) to walk the compromise; offer to follow with tracked redline and DocuSign if they accept. Lauren — please pre-stage the DocuSign envelope and flag Finance to confirm insurance coordination. Markus — if BlueWave asks for removal of the cap entirely, escalate to you for leadership sign-off.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
